- When sentiment is consistently low (0.00–0.33) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior period), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above prior peak for next 3–5 periods.  
- If sentiment is high (≥0.67) and price is trending up, model frequently overcorrects; apply downward bias of 1–3% to forecast if sentiment >0.75.  
- If model forecast is >10% above true outcome for 2+ consecutive periods, apply mean reversion: subtract 1–2% from next forecast if sentiment remains neutral or negative.  
- When sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, 0.00, 0.67), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with 1–2 day lag of true price movement.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is >85% of model’s 30d forecast, reduce forecast by 2–5% to avoid overconfidence bias.
